previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old male with a history of chronic pancreatitis, type 2 diabetes, PTSD, bipolar disorder, and prior abdominal surgeries was admitted for worsening pain, nausea, and vomiting due to a new incisional hernia. The hernia was reducible, and imaging showed no bowel obstruction or strangulation. He was managed conservatively with manual reduction, bowel rest, IV fluids, and pain control. His diet was gradually advanced, and he tolerated oral intake well. Pain was controlled with transition to oral hydromorphone. He remained stable, ambulatory, and was discharged home with instructions to follow up for elective hernia repair. All chronic medications were continued, and discharge planning included activity restrictions and warning signs to monitor.
problems: Incisional hernia without mention of obstruction or gangrene
Diabetes mellitus without mention of complication, type II or unspecified type, not stated as uncontrolled

Brief Hospital Course:
The patient with recurrent incisional hernia was admitted to the 
General Surgical Service for elective repair. On ___, the 
patient underwent repair of recurrent incarcerated incisional 
hernia with mesh, which went well without complication (reader 
referred to the Operative Note for details). After a brief, 
uneventful stay in the PACU, the patient arrived on the floor on 
clear liquid diet, on IV fluids, with a foley catheter, and 
Dilaudid PCA for pain control.  The patient was hemodynamically 
stable.
Neuro: The patient received Dilaudid PCA for pain control, IV 
Toradol was added on POD # 1 for better pain control. When 
tolerating oral intake, the patient was transitioned to oral 
pain medications and continued PCA until POD # 4. The PCA was 
discontinued on POD # 4 am, the patient was continued on PO 
Dilaudid, Tylenol and Motrin with adequate pain control.
CV: The patient remained stable from a cardiovascular 
standpoint; vital signs were routinely monitored.
Pulmonary: The patient remained stable from a pulmonary 
standpoint; vital signs were routinely monitored. Good pulmonary 
toilet, early ambulation and incentive spirrometry were 
encouraged throughout hospitalization.
GI: Post-operatively, the patient was started on clears with IV 
fluids. Diet was advanced when appropriate, which was well 
tolerated.  Patient's intake and output were closely monitored, 
and IV fluid was adjusted when necessary.  Electrolytes were 
routinely followed, and repleted when necessary.
GU: The foley catheter was discontinued at midnight of POD# 1. 
The patient subsequently voided without problem.
ID: The patient had a white blood count of 17.7 immediately post 
op, he remained afebrile during the entire hospitalization. 
Wound was found to have some blanching erythema around staples 
line, the patient was started on PO Kefzol. The wound was 
evaluated daily, no drainage or exudate was noticed. JP drain 
was removed prior discharge.
Endocrine: The patient's blood sugar was monitored throughout 
his stay; insulin dosing was adjusted accordingly.
Hematology: The patient's complete blood count was examined 
routinely; no transfusions were required.
Prophylaxis: The patient received subcutaneous heparin and 
venodyne boots were used during this stay; was encouraged to get 
up and ambulate as early as possible.
At the time of discharge, the patient was doing well, afebrile 
with stable vital signs.  The patient was tolerating a regular 
diabetic diet, ambulating, voiding without assistance, and pain 
was well controlled.  The patient received discharge teaching 
and follow-up instructions with understanding verbalized and 
agreement with the discharge plan.

Discharge Instructions:

weights greater than ___ lbs until you follow-up with your 
surgeon, who will instruct you further regarding activity 
restrictions.

and warm water.  Gently pat the area dry.

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  A ___ man with right internal jugular central venous line
placement.

COMPARISON:  Chest radiograph from ___.

ONE VIEW OF THE CHEST:

The lungs are low in volume and show a new right upper lobe opacity.  The
trachea is shifted to the right.  The cardiomediastinal silhouette and hilar
contours are normal.  No pleural effusion or pneumothorax is present.  A right
IJ catheter terminates in the right atrium and should be withdrawn.

IMPRESSION:

Low lung volumes with new right upper lobe collapse and a right internal
jugular catheter, which terminates in the right atrium.

These findings were not communicated to the primary team as the subsequent
film that was available at the time of review showed the internal jugular line
to be in the proximal SVC.

INDICATION:  ___ man with new line just moved back 6 cm.

COMPARISON:  Chest radiograph from ___ at 1:00 p.m.

ONE VIEW OF THE CHEST:

The lungs are well expanded and show a residual plate-like atelectasis in the
right upper lobe with reexpansion of the remaining lobe.  The
cardiomediastinal silhouette and hilar contours are normal.  No pleural
effusion or pneumothorax is present.  A right IJ catheter terminates in the
proximal SVC.

IMPRESSION:

Interval reinflation of the right upper lobe with the right internal jugular
line terminating in the proximal SVC.
